newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB Report-Tender may cap local wheat price.
newsitem.headline: AWB Report-Tender may cap local wheat price.

text.p: Australia's domestic grains market remains quiet with the Queensland sorghum harvest all but complete, the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said in its weekly grain market report.
The sorghum price remains steady at around A$145.00 a tonne delivered Brisbane, it said.
The Victorian market continues to provide the lead for most domestic grain trade, reflecting demand from the dairy sector, AWB said.

The sale of a parcel of 5,000 tonnes of wheat through the AWB domestic tender system will increase supplies into the domestic market and may present a ceiling to domestic prices in the short-term, AWB said.
Australian wheat shipments in the week to April 7 amounted to 268,414 tonnes, AWB confirmed.
This increased shipments to 10.54 million tonnes so far this shipping year, up on the 7.19 million tonnes shipped at the same time last year.

Internationally, Algeria was reported to buy 50,000 tonnes of French wheat at A$180.00 cost and freight for May shipment while Syria sold 50,000 tonnes of durum to Cyprus at A$195.00 a tonne for May shipment.
